aspects.fertilizer:
Punjab Varieties:
CPF-246 suits all Punjab districts except riverine areas, yielding 1050 maunds per acre with 12.15 percent sugar and high fertilizer tolerance. HSMF-242 and SPSG-1283 give good yields with average fertilizer on medium fertility soils.

Organic Manures:
Apply 3 to 4 trolleys, or 300 to 400 maunds, per acre of well-rotted farmyard manure. Raw manure increases termites; use 4 to 5 poison traps per acre. Alternatively, green manure with guar, jhanter, berseem, or senji, adding half bag urea per acre and burying at flowering 30 to 35 days before planting. Apply dry filter cake at 3 to 4 trolleys per acre one month before planting.

Plant Crop Fertilizer Doses:
In poor soils with organic matter up to 0., phosphorus up to 7 ppm, and potash up to 80 ppm, apply 120 kg nitrogen, 69 kg phosphorus, and 50 kg potash per acre, equal to 4 bags urea, 3 bags DAP, and 2 bags SOP.
In medium soils with organic matter 0. to 1., phosphorus 7 to 14 ppm, and potash 80 to 180 ppm, apply 103 kg nitrogen, 57 kg phosphorus, and 50 kg potash per acre, equal to 3.5 bags urea, 2.5 bags DAP, and 2 bags SOP.
In rich soils with organic matter above 1., phosphorus above 14 ppm, and potash above 180 ppm, apply 87 kg nitrogen, 46 kg phosphorus, and 38 kg potash per acre, equal to 3 bags urea, 2 bags DAP, and 1.5 bags SOP.
Apply 6 kg per acre of 33 percent zinc sulphate at planting for zinc deficiency.

Application Method and Timing:
Plant setts in furrows 4 feet apart and 10 to 12 inches deep. Apply all phosphorus, one-fourth nitrogen, and half potash in furrows at planting, and apply the remaining potash at earthing up. Potash and timely irrigation reduce frost damage in September planting.
Apply remaining nitrogen in three splits. For September planting, apply one month after planting, late March, and April. For spring planting, apply in April, late May, and late June at earthing up. Never apply nitrogen after August.

Ratoon Crop:
Ratoon requires 30 percent more nitrogen than a plant crop. Harvest plant crop after January 15 below ground level; do not ratoon diseased crops.
Per acre ratoon doses: poor soil takes 156 kg nitrogen, 69 kg phosphorus, and 50 kg potash (5.5 bags urea, 3 DAP, 2 SOP); medium soil takes 134 kg nitrogen, 57 kg phosphorus, and 50 kg potash (5 bags urea, 2.5 DAP, 2 SOP); rich soil takes 113 kg nitrogen, 46 kg phosphorus, and 38 kg potash (4 bags urea, 2 DAP, 1.5 SOP).
At wattar moisture, apply all phosphorus, potash, and one-third nitrogen along rows. Apply remaining nitrogen in April and late June at earthing up.

Nutrient Sources and App:
Per 50 kg bag, Urea provides 23 kg nitrogen (46 percent), CAN provides 13 kg nitrogen (26 percent), DAP provides 9 kg nitrogen and 23 kg phosphorus (18 percent nitrogen, 46 percent phosphorus), Nitrophos provides 11 kg nitrogen and 10 kg phosphorus (22 percent nitrogen, 20 percent phosphorus), SSP provides 9 kg phosphorus (18 percent), TSP provides 23 kg phosphorus (46 percent), SOP provides 25 kg potash (50 percent), and MOP provides 30 kg potash (60 percent). Soil Fertility Research Institute Punjab Lahore provides the free Khaad Hisab mobile app.
aspects.harvesting:
**Harvesting Operations:**
Sugarcane harvesting occurs from December to February.
Harvest September sown crop the following year in October, followed by February sown crop.
Harvest September sown, ratoon, early maturing, flood affected, rat damaged, and lodged crops first, then mid and late maturing crops.
Cut cane 0.5 to 1 inch below ground level to destroy borer larvae and help underground eyes sprout.
Transport cane to mills immediately after harvest to prevent loss in weight and recovery.
Never burn trash. Chop and incorporate it into the soil using a trash mulcher to maintain fertility and protect beneficial insects.

**Ratoon Management:**
Cut cane after January 15 if keeping ratoon.
Late January to early March is best for keeping ratoon crops.
Do not keep ratoon from crops cut in November, December, or early January due to frost killing eyes and causing gaps.
Fill gaps in ratoon crops using a separate nursery.
Clear trash and irrigate ratoon fields in February and March.
Apply 30 percent more nitrogen fertilizer to ratoon than fresh crops.
Never ratoon diseased crops or fields heavily infested with Gurdaspur borer.
Harvest diseased crops by December 15, plow the field, destroy residues, and sow a new variety after March 15.

**Irrigation and Field Care:**
Stop irrigation approximately one month before harvest.
Shorten irrigation intervals during frost, avoid hoeing, and plant in north-south furrows in frost-prone areas.
Bury empty pesticide containers in a pit away from food and children.

**Pest and Disease Management:**
Strip trash by hand instead of sickles to protect buds.
If sowing is delayed, cover seed with trash and sprinkle water intermittently.
In April or May, cut dried deadheart shoots at ground level and bury them.
In July or August, inspect for Gurdaspur borer, then cut attacked stalks 2 to 3 internodes below damage to feed animals or bury.
For red rot, plant resistant varieties in well drained soils, rotate crops, and destroy diseased plants with stubble.
Dip setts for 15 to 20 minutes in Azoxystrobin plus Clothianidin at 2 to 2.5 grams per liter of water, or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2 milliliters per liter of water.

**Punjab Sugar Mills:**

Al-Arabia Abdullah Shahpur Sargodha capacity is 12,000 tons.

aspects.irrigation:
**General Irrigation:**
February-planted sugarcane requires 64 acre-inches of water.
September-planted sugarcane requires 80 acre-inches of water.
Sugarcane requires 16 to 20 irrigations annually depending on rain and weather.
Apply light initial irrigation so roots penetrate deeply, plant growth improves, and lodging decreases.
Stop irrigation about one month before harvesting based on weather and soil type.

**Monthly Schedule:**
March to April: Apply 2 to 3 irrigations with intervals of 20 to 30 days.
May to June: Apply 5 to 6 irrigations with intervals of 10 to 12 days.
July to August: Apply 3 to 4 irrigations with intervals of 15 to 20 days.
September to October: Apply 2 to 3 irrigations with intervals of 20 to 30 days.
November to February: Apply 4 irrigations with intervals of 30 days.

**Water Quality:**
Suitable water has EC under 750, SAR under 2, and RSC under 0.75, usable without alteration.
Good water has EC 750 to 1250, SAR 2 to 6, and RSC 0.75 to 1.25, mixed with canal water every second irrigation.
Marginally good water has EC 1250 to 2250, SAR 6 to 10, and RSC 1.25 to 2.50, usable only mixed with canal water and required soil gypsum.
Unsuitable water has EC above 2250, SAR above 10, or RSC above 2.5, requiring agriculture department expert consultation before use.

**Planting and Moisture Management:**
Plant setts in two lines within 10 to 12 inches deep furrows spaced 4 feet apart.
Apply light water to furrows after planting, and irrigate again when furrows dry.
In riverine flood areas, plant spring sugarcane early and avoid May planting after wheat.
Spray S-metolachlor at 960 to 1000 ml per acre in moist soil 1 to 2 days after planting.
Spray mesotrione plus atrazine plus halosulfuron-methyl 80 at 500 grams per acre using 100 to 120 liters of water within one month of germination.
Irrigate one week after herbicide spraying, and hoe with a rotary machine three weeks later.
Level fields to prevent standing water.
Drain excess water during heavy rainfall.

**Extreme Weather and Pest Protection:**
Irrigate abundantly during severe heat of 47 degrees Celsius or higher.
Shorten irrigation intervals during frost, and irrigate according to weather forecasts.
Do not hoe during frost days, and plant north-to-south furrows in frost-prone areas.
Keep fields moist to prevent termite attacks, and apply 4 to 5 poisoned traps per acre.
Spray water twice weekly in patches against red mites.
Harvest ratoon crops after January 15, cutting 0.5 to 1 inch below ground level.
aspects.machinery:
Land Preparation:
Mix previous crop residue into the soil using a rotavator or disc harrow.
Plough twice with a soil-turning plough and level the land.
Plough 3 to 4 times with a common plough to make the soil crumbly.
Run a deep plough once every 3 years.
Sugarcane planters are available for mechanized planting to reduce labour and production costs.

Weed Control and Interculture Machinery:
The first hoeing should be done after emergence completes and the second hoeing one month later.
Plough in moist and dry conditions during each hoeing.
Use a cultivator to remove weeds between furrows.
Use a kasola or khurpa to remove weeds between plants.
Run a rotary weeder or small rotavator when the crop is approximately 2 months old.
Earth up soil around roots after the last hoeing to control weeds and prevent lodging.
Rotate crops with berseem or sorghum to reduce weeds.

Chemical Weed Control Machinery:
For pre-emergence spray, use S-metolachlor 960 at 1000 ml per acre 1 to 2 days after sowing in moist soil.
Use a flood jet or deflector nozzle for pre-emergence spray.
Run a cultivator between rows 45 to 50 days after pre-emergence spraying and earth up 100 days after spraying.
If not sprayed at sowing, apply post-emergence spray within one month of emergence using mesotrione plus atrazine plus halosulfuron-methyl 80 at 500 grams per acre.
Use a flat fan or T-jet nozzle for post-emergence spray.
Irrigate 1 week after post-emergence spray, and 3 weeks after spray perform hoeing using a rotary and earth up.
Use 100 to 120 liters of water per acre.
Fill the spray machine halfway with water, mix the herbicide, and add the remaining water.
Calibrate water volume by spraying a test area to calculate total tanks per acre and divide the herbicide equally.
Do not use sprayed weeds as fodder.
Wash the spray machine thoroughly after use.
Preferably use separate spray machines for herbicides and insecticides.

Trash Management Machinery:
Harvest according to variety and maturity, and deliver cane to the mill without delay.
Do not burn trash after harvest.
Use a trash mulcher machine to chop trash and mix it into the soil to improve soil fertility and reduce air pollution.
In February and March, clear trash from the field and irrigate.

Ratoon and Pest Control Machinery:
Do not keep ratoon from diseased crops.
Harvest diseased crops by December 15, plough the field, destroy residues, and plant a new variety after March 15.
Dip cutting tools in detergent powder or Dettol and wash hands with soap.
For borer control, rotavate stubbles before March if ratoon is not kept.
In April or May, cut dried shoots at ground level and bury them.
Install light traps from March to October.
Apply 20 to 25 beneficial insect cards per acre.
aspects.other:
**Land Preparation:**
Select heavy loam soil. Mix previous crop residues into soil using a rotavator or disc harrow, or dispose of residues separately. Plow twice with a soil-inverting plow and level the land. Plow 3 to 4 times with a common plow to pulverize the soil. Plow deeply once every 3 years. Level the field to prevent standing water and ensure uniform plant nutrition.

**Sowing and Seed Rate:**
Spring sowing is from February 15 to the end of March. September sowing is from September 1 to October 15. Treat seed with fungicide before sowing. Planting requires 60,000 buds per acre, obtained from 30,000 two-bud setts or 20,000 three-bud setts. Seed rate by weight is 100 to 120 maunds per acre. Sugarcane crop from 12 to 16 marlas is sufficient to plant 1 acre.

**Intercropping:**
In September-sown sugarcane, intercrop short-duration canola, toria, raya, mustard, wheat, lentils, gram, or garlic. This increases farmer income and soil fertility while protecting against frost.

**Crop Management:**
Earth up soil around roots after the final hoeing to control weeds and prevent lodging. Earth up stubbles in May or June to prevent Gurdaspur borer moths from emerging. Drain excess water from fields during excessive rain. Irrigate according to crop needs during drought and high temperatures.

**Frost Protection:**
Severe frost reduces cane weight, juice sweetness, and eye sprouting for the next crop seed. Apply potassium fertilizer to increase plant tolerance to cold and heat. Irrigate according to weather forecasts. Avoid hoeing during frost days. Plant sugarcane in north-south furrows in frost-prone areas. Deliver harvested sugarcane to mills without delay.

aspects.overview:
General:
Sugarcane matures in nearly a full year and produces sugar, gur, and shakkar. Well-drained heavy loam soil is best. Irrigated loam and light loam are suitable. Saline and sandy soils are unsuitable. Deep plow and level the land. Spring sowing is 15 February to end March. September sowing is 1 September to 15 October. Seed rate is 100 to 120 maunds per acre, treated with fungicide. Inspect fields in the first 60 days to cut and bury diseased plants. Pest generations emerge in May, May, July, and August, causing leaf holes, bunchy tops, and overwintering as caterpillars in cane tops.

Ratoon Management:
Ratoon covers 41 percent of Punjab sugarcane area. Prefer spring-planted ratoon. Keep ratoon late January to early March and harvest after 15 January below ground level. Avoid keeping ratoon from diseased fields or during November to January. Fill gaps using a separate nursery. Apply 30 percent more nitrogen fertilizer than a fresh crop.

Punjab Statistics:
2020-21: 776.98 thousand hectares, 1920 thousand acres, 57,000 thousand metric tons, 742 maunds per acre average yield.
2021-22: 869.25 thousand hectares, 2148 thousand acres, 64,245 thousand metric tons, 748 maunds per acre.
2022-23: 938.04 thousand hectares, 2318 thousand acres, 66,932 thousand metric tons, 722 maunds per acre.
2023-24: 800.00 thousand hectares, 1977 thousand acres, 63,309 thousand metric tons, 801 maunds per acre.
2024-25 second estimate: 816.64 thousand hectares, 2018 thousand acres, 61,347 thousand metric tons, 760 maunds per acre.

Punjab Varieties:
CP 400-77: 900 maunds per acre, 11.90 percent sugar, early maturing, for all districts including riverine areas.
SPF-213: 900 maunds, 10.50 percent sugar, mid-maturing, for all districts.
CPF-237: 950 maunds, 12.50 percent sugar, early, lodging resistant, for all districts.
HSF-240: 950 maunds, 11.70 percent sugar, mid-maturing, red rot tolerant, smut susceptible, for all districts.
SPF-234: 1000 maunds, 11.60 percent sugar, low red rot resistance, South Punjab except riverine areas.
HSMF-242: 1020 maunds, 12.50 percent sugar, mid-maturing, for all districts except riverine.
CPF-246: 1050 maunds, 12.15 percent sugar, tolerates high fertilizer, all districts except riverine.
CPF-247: 1050 maunds, 12.25 percent sugar.
CPF-248: 1120 maunds, 12.71 percent sugar.
CPF-249: 1160 maunds, 12.46 percent sugar.
CPF-250: 1113 maunds, 12.72 percent sugar, early maturing.
CPF-251: 1080 maunds, 13.20 percent sugar, early, suited for low fertility soil.
CPF-252: 1298 maunds, 11.70 percent sugar, late maturing, suited for September sowing and ratoon, all districts.
CPF-253: 1167 maunds, 12.54 percent sugar, mid-maturing.
SPSG-1283: 1180 maunds, 12.30 percent sugar, mid-maturing.
CPSG-2525: 1150 maunds, highest sugar at 13.30 percent.
YTFG-236: 1290 maunds, 12.73 percent sugar, very early maturing.

Inactive: Brothers Kasur, Imperial Colony Mandi Bahauddin, Haseeb Waqas Rahim Yar Khan.
aspects.pests_diseases:
**Punjab:**
CP 400-77 yields 900 maunds per acre with 11.90 percent sugar and resists pests and diseases.
Biological control laboratories in 11 districts provide free Chrysoperla and Trichogramma cards.
Plant early spring cane in riverine areas and avoid May planting after wheat.

**Southern Punjab:**
Sugarcane pink mealybug females lay up to 1000 eggs hatching in 10 to 14 hours.
Spray Profenofos 500 SC at 800 mL, Methidathion 50 EC at 500 mL, or Imidacloprid 200 SL at 250 mL per 100 liters water.

**Variety Restrictions:**
HSF-240 is susceptible to smut.
SPF-234 has low red rot resistance.
Fakhr-e-Hind, CO-1148, and COJ-84 are cancelled due to red rot.
SPF-238 is cancelled due to borers.
NSG-59 is cancelled due to late tillering.
L-118, CO-975, CPL-54, BF-162, COL-44, and COL-29 lost yield potential.

**Planting and Seed Treatment:**
Soak setts 15 to 20 minutes in Azoxystrobin plus Clothianidin at 2 to 2.5 grams per liter, or Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2 mL per liter water.
Make 10 to 12 inch deep furrows spaced 4 feet apart.
Place two sett lines 9 inches apart and cover with 1 to 1.5 inches soil.
Harvest ratoon after January 15 below ground level.
Apply 30 percent more nitrogen to ratoon crops.

**Disease Management:**
Red rot Colletotrichum falcatum causes hollow red pith with white patches.
Never keep ratoon from fields infected with red rot, smut, or white leaf disease.
For white leaf disease, harvest by December 15, plow the field, and plant a new variety after March 15.

**Insect Pests:**
Flood Chlorpyrifos 40 EC at 2 liters or Fipronil SC at 1 to 1.5 liters per acre for termites, or use 4 to 5 poisoned traps per acre.
Apply Chlorantraniliprole 0.4 G at 8 kg or Fipronil 0.3 G at 8 to 9 kg per acre at 45, 90, and 120 days after planting for borers.
Install light traps March to October.
Release 20 to 25 beneficial insect cards per acre monthly from April to October.
Earth up stubbles in May or June.
For pyrilla, spray Bifenthrin EC at 250 mL or Dimethoate 40 EC at 400 mL per acre.
For black bug, spray Imidacloprid plus Fipronil WG at 60 grams or Bifenthrin 10 EC at 300 mL per acre.
For whitefly, spray Pyriproxyfen 10.8 EC at 500 mL, Spirotetramat 240 SC at 125 mL, Flonicamid 50 WG at 80 grams, or Pyrifluquinazon 20 WG at 200 grams per acre.
For mites, spray Spiromesifen plus Emamectin SC at 100 mL or Fenpyroximate SC at 200 mL per acre.

**Animal Pests:**
Treat rat burrows with Zinc phosphide dough balls or one Aluminium phosphide tablet.
Bait rats with 1 kg boiled wheat, 25 grams Zinc phosphide, 25 mL edible oil, and 100 grams molasses.
Fumigate porcupine burrows with 20 to 30 Phosphine or Detia gas tablets.
Control wild boars using hunting dogs or poison baits.

**Spraying Guidelines:**
Use 100 to 120 liters water per acre.
Use flood jet or deflector nozzles before emergence.
Use flat fan or T-jet nozzles after emergence.
aspects.sowing:
All Punjab Districts:
CPF-252 yields an average of 1298 maunds per acre with 11.70 percent sugar. It is late-maturing and suitable for September planting and ratooning. Plant HSF-240 on less area because it is susceptible to disease.

Sowing Times:
Spring sowing is from 15 February to 31 March.
September sowing is from 1 September, or 15 September, to 15 October.
Because September temperatures exceed 37 degrees Celsius and harm germination, September planting is recommended from late September to late October.

Riverine and Flood-Prone Areas:
Sow early spring sugarcane.
Avoid planting sugarcane in May after wheat.

Weather Stress Management:
Irrigate frequently during severe heat of 47 degrees Celsius or higher to avoid leaf scorching and mite attacks.
In frost-prone areas, plant in north-south furrows.
Avoid hoeing during frost days.
Deliver harvested cane to the mill without delay.

Soil and Field Preparation:
Heavy loam soil is best.
Deep plough once every 3 years.
Incorporate crop residues using a rotavator or disc harrow, or dispose of them separately.
Level the land to avoid standing water.
Plough twice with a mouldboard plough, followed by 3 to 4 normal ploughings.
If farm manure is unavailable, sow guar, jantar, berseem, or senji as green manure.
Bury green manure at flowering, apply half a bag of urea per acre, and wait 30 to 35 days before land preparation.

Seed Preparation:
Seed rate is 100 to 120 maunds per acre.
Treat seed with fungicide.
Select seed from plant crops, though ratoon crops can be used for September planting.
Use the upper portion of cane for seed and send the lower portion to the mill.
Do not select seed from lodged or frost-affected crops.
Strip dry leaves by hand instead of sickles to protect eye buds.
Remove leaf sheaths to prevent termite attacks and poor germination.
Plant immediately, or cover seed with trash and sprinkle water intermittently.

Sowing Method:
Make 10 to 12 inch deep furrows spaced 4 feet apart using a ridger.
Place two rows of sets 9 inches apart, end-to-end.
Apply recommended fertilizer and granular poison or spray over sets.
Cover sets with 1 to 1.5 inches of soil by hand or foot.
Apply light irrigation, and irrigate again when trenches dry.
Mechanical sugarcane planters can be used.
Earth up around plant bases in May or June to prevent Gurdaspur borer moths.

Ratoon Crop:
Keep ratoon crops from late January to early March.
Avoid keeping ratoon from November to January.
Fill gaps using a nursery.
Never keep ratoon from diseased crops.
Harvest diseased crops by 15 December, plough residues, and sow a new variety after 15 March.
aspects.varieties:
Sowing Dates:
Spring sowing runs from 15 February to late March. September sowing runs from 1 September to 15 October, preferring HSF-240, SPF-213, CPF-246, and CPF-252.

All Punjab Varieties:
CP 400-77 matures early, yields 900 maunds per acre, has 11.90 percent sugar, and suits all districts including riverine areas and Lahore plains.
SPF-213 matures medium, yields 900 maunds per acre, and has 10.50 percent sugar.
CPF-237 matures early, yields 950 maunds per acre, has 12.50 percent sugar, and resists lodging.
HSF-240 matures medium, yields 950 maunds per acre, has 11.70 percent sugar, resists red rot, but contracts whip smut, requiring small-scale planting.
CPF-252 matures late, yields 1298 maunds per acre, has 11.70 percent sugar, and suits September planting and ratooning.

Southern and Non-Riverine Punjab:
HSMF-242 yields 1020 maunds per acre with 12.50 percent sugar on average fertilizer in all districts except riverine areas.
CPF-246 yields 1050 maunds per acre with 12.15 percent sugar and tolerates high fertilizer in non-riverine districts.
SPF-234 yields 1000 maunds per acre with 11.60 percent sugar in Southern Punjab excluding riverine areas, but has low red rot resistance.

Other Approved Varieties:
YTF-G-236 matures very early, yielding 1290 maunds per acre with 12.73 percent sugar.
CPF-250 matures early, yielding 1113 maunds per acre with 12.72 percent sugar.
CPF-251 matures early, yields 1080 maunds per acre, has 13.20 percent sugar, and suits low-fertility soils.
CPF-247 yields 1050 maunds per acre with 12.25 percent sugar.
CPF-248 yields 1120 maunds per acre with 12.71 percent sugar.
CPF-249 yields 1160 maunds per acre with 12.46 percent sugar.
CPF-253 matures medium, yielding 1167 maunds per acre with 12.54 percent sugar.
Conditionally approved CPSG-2525 yields 1150 maunds per acre with the highest sugar at 13.30 percent.
Conditionally approved SLSG-1283 or SPSG-1283 matures medium, yielding 1180 maunds per acre with 12.30 percent sugar on average fertilizer.

Disapproved Varieties:
Do not plant NSG-59, Co-1148, CoJ-84, Co-975, L-118, CPL-54, BF-162, COL-44, COL-29, L-116, SPF-238, or Fakhr-e-Hind due to red rot, borers, delayed tillering, or yield loss.

Planting and Seed Rate:
Plant in heavy loam soil using 4-foot deep furrows with two sett lines 9 inches apart, covering setts with 1 to 1.5 inches of soil.
Seed rate is 100 to 120 maunds, 12 to 16 marlas, or 60,000 buds per acre using 30,000 two-bud or 20,000 three-bud setts.
Strip trash by hand.
Dip setts 15 to 20 minutes in Azoxystrobin plus Clothianidin at 2 to 2.5 grams per liter, Azoxystrobin plus Difenoconazole at 2 milliliters per liter, or Thiophanate-methyl or Fosetyl-aluminium at 2 to 2.5 grams per liter of water.

Crop Management:
Use floodjet or deflector nozzles pre-emergence, and flat fan or T-jet nozzles post-emergence.
Do not ratoon diseased or lodged crops.
Harvest diseased fields by 15 December, plow, and sow new varieties after 15 March.
aspects.weeds:
Yield Losses and Weeds:
Weeds can reduce sugarcane yield by up to 25 percent.
Spring crop weeds include bathu, bili booti, jangli cholai, jangli palak, jangli halon, karand, dumbi sitti, it-sit, morak, karabara, deela, khabal, naroo, kulfa, gajar booti, sainji, and lehli.
September planted crop weeds include it-sit, deela, jangli swank, dhandan, lomar ghas, makro, madhana, hazar dani, swanki, tandla, kulfa, and cholai.
Other common weeds include bathu, deela, and jangli jai.
Ratoon crop weeds include khabbal, barru, and madhana.
Keeping fields free of weeds prevents whitefly attacks during high humidity.

Non-Chemical Weed Control:
Crop rotation with fodder crops like berseem or sorghum eliminates or reduces weeds.
Hoeing is the best method to destroy weeds, soften soil, and spread roots.
Do the first hoeing after germination completes and the second hoeing one month later.
Plow once in moist soil condition and once in dry soil condition during each hoeing.
Use a cultivator or rotavator between rows, and use a kasola or khurpa between plants.
Run a rotary weeder or small rotavator when the crop is about 2 months old.
Earth up soil around roots after the final hoeing to control weeds and prevent lodging.
In February and March, clear dry trash from the field and apply water.
Do not burn trash. Chop and mix trash into the soil, or use a trash mulcher machine.
Plant pest-free and disease-free seed, and peel leaf sheaths off setts before planting.

Pre-Emergence Weed Control:
Spray S-metolachlor 960 at 960 to 1000 ml per acre in moist soil 1 to 2 days after planting.
Use a flood jet or deflector nozzle for pre-emergence spray.
Run a cultivator between rows 45 to 50 days after spraying.
Earth up soil 100 days after spraying.

Post-Emergence Weed Control:
If no herbicide was used at planting, spray mesotrione plus atrazine plus halosulfuron-methyl 80 at 500 grams per acre within one month of germination.
Use a flat fan or T-jet nozzle for post-emergence spray.
In warm weather, use mesotrione, atrazine, and topramezone.
Irrigate 1 week after spraying.
Hoe with a rotary weeder 3 weeks after spraying.
Earth up soil 90 to 100 days after spraying.

Ratoon Sugarcane:
From mid-March to mid-April, spray a mixture of mesotrione 1000 ml, atrazine 35 ml, and topramezone per acre.
Plow 3 weeks after spraying.
Earth up soil around roots 8 weeks after spraying.

Herbicide Precautions:
Do not hoe immediately after spraying, as it breaks chemical action and airborne chemical dust damages farmer health.
Do not feed sprayed weeds to livestock.
Wash the spray machine thoroughly after use.
Use separate machines for weed sprays and insecticide sprays.

timing.sowing: 15 February to 31 March (spring) and 1 September to 15 October (September)
